name: Berecynthia

attributes.attribute: her white-veiled image passed through the fields in spring
possibly related to the goddess Brigindo

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Berecynthia is a Continental Celtic goddess. The early Christian writer Gregory of Tours gave the record of her. Her image, veiled in white, was carried through the fields each spring. The rite also ran when crops threatened to fail. She may be a form of the goddess Brigindo. Both act as regional fertility spirits. Martin of Tours destroyed most of the region's pagan idols. Because of this no image of Berecynthia is likely to survive.

okr.objective: Berecynthia is a scantily known Continental goddess carried through the fields as a white-veiled image each spring.
